name: Custom silicon (hyperscaler ASICs)
thesis: Hyperscalers are designing their way around Nvidia with bespoke accelerators — but only two firms can co-design them at scale, and they all funnel through the same TSMC nodes and CoWoS slots.

gauge.rationale: ASIC shipments now outgrowing merchant GPUs for the first time, with new programs (Apple, OpenAI, Anthropic) added — but the design duopoly and shared TSMC/CoWoS chokepoints keep it tight.

why_it_gates: Hyperscaler accelerators — Google TPU, Amazon Trainium, Meta MTIA, Microsoft Maia — are how the largest buyers cut their Nvidia dependence. But the hyperscalers don't build them alone: Broadcom and Marvell together do ~95% of the custom-ASIC co-design work, and every one of these chips is fabricated by TSMC on advanced nodes and assembled with CoWoS. So custom silicon doesn't escape the compute bottleneck — it inherits the same foundry and packaging chokepoints as merchant GPUs.

watchlist.name: Broadcom
watchlist.role: ~70%+ of custom-AI co-design; TPU/MTIA; six XPU customers

watchlist.name: TSMC
watchlist.role: Fabricates every hyperscaler ASIC — shared chokepoint

catalysts.text: MediaTek's first hyperscaler ASIC ramps; ~$2B revenue, double prior guidance
Broadcom targets $100B AI chip revenue (timing may slip to late 2027/2028 on TSMC capacity)
OpenAI, Anthropic, Apple custom programs move toward volume

what_loosens_it: A generational efficiency leap from Nvidia or AMD that undercuts the economics of building custom chips, or TSMC advanced-node and CoWoS capacity catching up. Neither looks likely to bite before mid-2027, which is when TSMC constraints are expected to ease.

developments.text: TrendForce: custom ASIC shipments to grow 44.6% in 2026 vs 16.1% for merchant GPUs
Broadcom Q1 FY26 AI revenue $8.4B (+106% YoY); confirms six XPU customers including Apple, OpenAI, Anthropic
MediaTek doubles AI-ASIC guidance to ~$2B for Q4 2026; second program targeting 2027 mass production
